derivationStages.stageRecord: This analysis takes قرأ as the active perfect verb ‘read’, الطلاب as ‘the students’, and الكتاب as ‘the book’. Each nominal is constructed by externally merging the definite article with its noun. The article is represented as D and the remaining nominal material as N; their lexical characters jointly supply the written word without any additional realization operation. The definiteness relations connect each article to its nominal restriction. The verb selects an internal theme argument; its reader argument will be introduced by agentive v.
derivationStages.statement: Select the ordinary lexical reading and construct the two definite nominals.

values.surfaceStatus: case vowels are not written in the input

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the verb externally merges with ‘the book’, assigning that DP the theme role. Agentive v then merges with the resulting VP and licenses accusative on the object. Finally, ‘the students’ merges at the edge of the v projection and receives the external reader role. The labels VP and vP identify the projecting heads of these bare-structure sets; the intermediate v projection does not introduce an additional lexical head. The subject remains inside the verbal domain, a commitment needed for the eventual verb–subject–object order.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the transitive predicate with a low subject.

values.pronunciation: higher V occurrence pronounced; lower V occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb internally merges with v from its previously established VP position. This creates a complex v head containing a higher occurrence of the verb and the silent agentive head. The two verb occurrences share one lexical identity. The lower V occurrence becomes unpronounced, while the higher occurrence retains the input form قرأ. This local head-movement step precedes movement of the complex head to T.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the lexical verb to agentive v.

values.configuration: postverbal subject; no nominal raising to the T edge

values.surfaceStatus: case vowels are not written in the input

derivationStages.stageRecord: Perfect finite T externally merges with the established vP. T agrees with the low subject in person and gender; this analysis implements the Arabic postverbal agreement pattern with default singular number, rather than matching the plural subject in number. Thus the verb has third-person masculine singular agreement despite the plural students. T also licenses nominative on that subject. T has no requirement here to move a nominal into its edge, so the subject stays in its earlier position. The written verb is treated as an already inflected lexical form; the silent T represents its syntactic tense and agreement features, not an additional pronounced word.
derivationStages.statement: Merge finite T and license the postverbal subject.

values.pronunciation: only the highest verb occurrence is pronounced

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex v head now internally merges with the previously introduced T. Its higher occurrence contains the pronounced verb, while the entire lower complex-head occurrence is silenced; the original VP occurrence of V remains silent as well. This completes the successive V-to-v-to-T dependency. With no nominal raising, the pronounced order is the T-hosted verb, the students in the vP edge, and the book in the complement of V. The result is the ordinary reading ‘The students read the book.’ The root is analyzed as a finite declarative TP; no independently motivated complementizer layer is added.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the ordinary VSO analysis: the students read the book.

cases.sentence: राम ने सीता की मदद की।

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge सीता with the following genitive K head की, forming a head-final K object. K assigns genitive to सीता; its feminine form will be checked against the noun it modifies, not against the sex of सीता. Independently introduce मदद as a feminine singular noun. The analysis uses category labels without bar levels: a merged object's label identifies its projecting head rather than an independently supplied phrase-structure template.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the genitive dependent and the feminine nominal predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge the genitive object to the left of मदद, with N projecting. In the ordinary helping interpretation, the genitive dependent identifies the target of the help. Thus सीता is inside the nominal constituent, not a separately case-marked verbal object. Establish concord between the genitive marker की and feminine singular मदद. No overt determiner or additional silent D layer is required for this bare nominal.
derivationStages.statement: Build सीता की मदद as the nominal component of the predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Introduce the light verb कर and merge the existing nominal as its complement, to its left. The resulting predicate means to provide help: मदद supplies the principal lexical content, while कर supplies the verbal component. This analysis retains the nominal as a syntactic constituent rather than incorporating मदद into a single lexical terminal. कर is retained here as the verb's lexical form; its perfective realization has not yet been established.
derivationStages.statement: Form the head-final noun–light-verb predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First merge the existing verbal object with an unpronounced transitive agentive v. Build the head-final subject constituent from राम and ने, then merge it at the edge of the v projection. Agentive v assigns the external Agent role to this subject. The overt ergative K form is selected here, but its licensing by the perfective transitive configuration is established at the next stage. The subject is now explicitly present in its first-merged position, from which it can subsequently move.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the external argument राम ने above the light-verb predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge perfective Asp above the existing transitive v object. In this analysis, perfective Asp together with transitive v licenses the subject's ergative K, ने. The ergative subject is unavailable to control verbal agreement, and the genitive dependent सीता की is likewise case-marked. Asp therefore agrees with the unmarked nominal complement सीता की मदद, whose head मदद supplies feminine singular features. With perfective aspect and those features established, the light verb कर and Asp receive the collective surface realization की. This final की is verbal and is distinct from the earlier genitive की. The realization association preserves the lexical verb कर in the syntax rather than replacing it with an unanalyzed surface verb.
derivationStages.statement: Establish perfective aspect, ergative licensing, and feminine singular verbal realization.

values.dependencyRepresentation: pronounced landing occurrence and silent source trace

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge an unpronounced finite T above the aspectual object, then internally merge the already established subject राम ने at the T edge to satisfy T's subject requirement. The landing occurrence retains the subject's identity; its earlier position is represented by an unpronounced K trace with the same lineage. This trace convention does not duplicate the subject's internal lexical material. Movement preserves the Agent interpretation and ergative case already established below. T contributes finiteness without an overt auxiliary, while the perfective light verb retains the realization की. The completed head-final T object consequently yields राम ने सीता की मदद की.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the finite clause by raising the ergative subject to the T edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines the noun kitabu with a phonologically null D, and then combines the resulting DP with nunua ‘buy’. The verb assigns its internal argument the Theme role. The null determiner does not impose an English-style definite or indefinite interpretation. Kitabu is retained as a whole noun, including its nominal class morphology. Projection labels such as VP and DP abbreviate the categories determined by their heads; they do not introduce an independent X-bar template.
derivationStages.statement: The verb combines with its class-7 internal argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A transitive v merges with the VP. Its object-agreement probe finds the accessible class-7 DP kitabu, and the valued agreement is represented by ki on v. The same transitive licensing domain assigns abstract accusative Case to that DP. This analysis treats ki as object agreement with the integrated lexical object, not as a second independently interpreted Theme argument.
derivationStages.statement: Transitive v licenses the object and its class-7 agreement marker.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The proper-name DP Juma externally merges with the existing v projection. It receives the Agent role in the external-argument position. The name is represented as a single DP terminal, without an additional pronounced determiner. Its human singular features provide the controller for the subject agreement introduced later.
derivationStages.statement: Juma is merged as the external argument.

values.pronunciation: The higher V occurrence is pronounced; the VP-internal occurrence is silent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The previously merged V nunua undergoes head movement to v. The resulting complex head places the object marker ki before the verb. The original V occurrence remains in the complement position but is now unpronounced; the new occurrence in the complex head is pronounced at this stage. This is a copy-theoretic head-movement commitment, rather than base generation of the whole inflected verb in one terminal.
derivationStages.statement: The lexical verb raises to the object-agreement-bearing v.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Past T merges above the external-argument projection. Its subject-agreement probe agrees with Juma, the highest accessible DP, yielding third-person singular class-1 agreement. Finite T licenses nominative Case on Juma. This analysis bundles subject agreement with T rather than introducing an independent agreement projection: the T terminal ali represents subject a- followed by past -li-. These are still only parts of the eventual written verb; their association with the complete input word is established after head movement to T.

values.pronunciation: The highest complex is pronounced; the lower v complex is silent.

relations.relation: extension of the lexical-verb copy chain

values.identity: All three occurrences instantiate the same lexical verb.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex v head shown in the preceding workspace raises to T. The T material precedes the copied v complex, giving the morphological sequence a-li-ki-nunua. The lower occurrence of the entire v complex becomes silent, including the V occurrence it contains; the still lower VP-internal V remains silent as well. The new highest complex is associated with the single written word alikinunua. This association records the collective spelling of the existing heads without replacing their syntax or making either lower copy pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: The verbal complex raises to T and receives its written realization.

values.pronunciation: The TP-edge occurrence is pronounced; the external-argument occurrence is silent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: T's EPP requirement triggers Internal Merge of Juma from the external-argument position already present in the preceding workspace. The new DP occurrence occupies the outer edge of TP, above the finite verbal complex. Its lower occurrence becomes silent. Agreement and nominative licensing were established before this movement; raising satisfies the positional requirement rather than creating a second Agent interpretation. With only the highest subject and verbal occurrences pronounced, the clause has the order Juma–alikinunua–kitabu.
derivationStages.statement: Juma raises to the preverbal subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative C merges with the completed TP, establishing a root declarative clause. No additional displacement or pronunciation change is required. The final structure interprets Juma as the buyer and kitabu as the purchased Theme in a past event. The postverbal DP remains the integrated complement of nunua; object agreement does not require treating it as a detached afterthought. The syntax leaves its precise definiteness or specificity to the interpretation of the object-agreement construction and context. The pronounced subject, the collectively realized finite verb, and the noun spell the exact input, with punctuation external to the syntactic terminals.
derivationStages.statement: A null declarative C completes the clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The Hausa sentence receives a monoclausal subject-focus analysis: Audu is the focused subject, ne is the overt focus head, ya is the third-person masculine singular relative-perfective auxiliary, and tafi is the lexical verb ‘go’. The interpretation is approximately ‘It is Audu who went.’ The proper name is treated as an atomic D that is also a maximal nominal, as permitted in Bare Phrase Structure. A silent verbalizing head introduces the external argument. These objects initially remain separate; the order of their introduction is not a claim about surface word order.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lexical resources for a subject-focus clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge first combines the silent verbalizing head with tafi. Audu then merges at the edge of that verbal projection. The resulting structure gives Audu the Actor role of the going event. No object is projected: tafi is used intransitively here. The projection labels identify the heads that determine the merged objects; they do not introduce independent phrase-structure templates.
derivationStages.statement: Build the verbal predicate and introduce Audu as its external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The auxiliary ya merges above the verbal phrase. It supplies perfective aspect in the relative paradigm used in this focus construction; this does not independently require a past-tense interpretation. T then agrees with the still-low subject Audu, valuing its subject agreement as third-person masculine singular and licensing the nominal's nominative Case. This analysis treats agreement as preceding subject raising, so the agreement relation targets the thematic occurrence that is present at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Merge the finite auxiliary and establish subject agreement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies Audu from the external-argument position already established inside the verbal phrase to the edge of the T projection. This satisfies the subject-edge requirement adopted for the finite clause. The landing occurrence is pronounced at this stage, while the thematic occurrence becomes silent. Both occurrences retain the identity of the same nominal; the lower occurrence continues to determine its thematic interpretation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the subject to the finite clause's subject position.

relations.relation: focus-construction licensing of the auxiliary paradigm

derivationStages.stageRecord: The focus head ne externally merges with the completed TP. In this analysis, ne heads a clause-peripheral focus projection rather than an independent copular clause containing a relative-clause predicate. The focus construction licenses the relative-perfective form ya in its finite complement. The subject has not yet moved into the focus projection, so its currently pronounced occurrence remains at the TP edge.
derivationStages.statement: Merge ne above the finite clause.

values.interpretation: Audu identifies the individual who went
values.pronunciation: highest occurrence pronounced; lower occurrences silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge moves Audu from the previously established TP-edge occurrence to the edge of the focus projection. This is the A-bar step that makes the subject the identificational focus: Audu identifies the individual who went, while the open proposition concerns someone going. The new highest occurrence is pronounced, and the TP-edge occurrence becomes silent, leaving both lower occurrences available for interpretation. The focus head ne is then identified as the masculine singular form associated with Audu. The completed clause is the maximal focus projection; no additional silent declarative C is required for this analysis. Its pronounced terminals, in order, are Audu, ne, ya, and tafi.
derivationStages.statement: Complete subject focus and derive Audu ne ya tafi.

relations.relation: Transitive selection and internal theta-role assignment

derivationStages.stageRecord: The input is Georgian: კაცმა is the ergative form of ‘man’, წერილი is the nominative form of ‘letter’, and დაწერა is the transitive aorist ‘wrote’. Each nominal projects an NP through N′; no unpronounced article or determiner is posited. The object NP combines with V to form V′, and the subject NP occupies Spec-VP. This establishes the verb’s two-place argument structure: the object receives Theme and the VP-internal subject receives Agent. A separate, unpronounced finite I head bears Series II/aorist features. The written verb is retained as one lexical terminal rather than decomposed into speculative morpheme boundaries. Its overt morphology is present, but its syntactic association with I has not yet been established.
derivationStages.statement: Construct a head-final VP with an Agent subject and a Theme object.

values.licensing: inherent Case associated with the external Agent in this Series II transitive configuration
structural Case on the governed internal argument in this Series II transitive configuration

derivationStages.stageRecord: VP combines with the head-final I to form I′, which projects IP; Spec-IP is not yet filled. I establishes the clause’s finite aorist specification. This analysis adopts a Series-sensitive Government and Binding implementation of Georgian Case: in the Series II transitive configuration, the lexical predicate licenses inherent ergative on its Agent and structural nominative on its internal argument. Accordingly, კაცმა is the ergative subject and წერილი the nominative object, not an accusative object inferred from English translation. Both Case relations are established at the arguments’ current VP positions, before either movement operation. The verb’s existing whole-word form expresses the finite aorist specification; this is not a separate pronunciation or an operation that rewrites the terminal.
derivationStages.statement: Project finite IP and license the Series II ergative–nominative Case pattern.

values.pronunciation: the raised lexical head is pronounced; its lower trace is silent

values.motivation: satisfaction of the finite clause's subject-position requirement
values.pronunciation: the raised NP is pronounced; its lower trace is silent

values.interpretation: one argument chain, with no additional theta-role at Spec-IP

values.headDependency: local head chain licenses the V trace
values.locality: both dependencies remain within the same finite clause
values.nominalDependency: the raised subject antecedent-governs its A-trace

derivationStages.stageRecord: The lexical V raises from its previously represented VP-internal position and adjoins to I, leaving a silent head trace. The resulting complex I hosts the finite verb დაწერა; the wordless inflectional component adds no separately pronounced terminal. The subject NP raises from the previously represented Spec-VP position to Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace. These movements have independent landing sites and do not require an intervening workspace: head movement associates V with finite I, while subject A-movement satisfies the clause’s subject-position requirement. Neither landing position receives a new theta-role. The subject chain retains the Agent role and ergative Case established below, and the object remains in its nominative-licensed complement position. The head trace is licensed by its local head chain, and the subject trace is antecedent-governed by the raised subject; neither dependency crosses an intervening clause or barrier. There is no anaphor or pronominal requiring a further Binding Theory dependency. No CP layer, topicalization, or covert determiner is required for this declarative. The pronounced order is exactly კაცმა წერილი დაწერა, with the interpretation ‘The/a man wrote the/a letter’; the definiteness alternatives do not require distinct structures here.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the clause through V-to-I movement and subject A-movement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Abafana is projected as an NP headed by a class-2 plural noun, and ibhola as an NP headed by a class-5 noun. The verb dlala selects a nominal theme and an external agent. The finite inflectional head contains class-2 subject concord ba- and affirmative present morphology ya-. This analysis treats the postverbal ibhola as the selected object of 'play'; it does not posit an otherwise unexpressed object pronoun or an afterthought structure. The analysis represents nominal arguments as NPs, a standard GB option, rather than adding silent determiners. The bound inflectional material is not yet combined with the verb.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lexical items and their inflectional properties.

relations.relation: Complement selection and internal theta-role assignment

values.interpretation: The ball or football activity is the internal argument of play.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Dlala first combines with ibhola as its NP complement, forming V′. The verb assigns its internal theme role to that NP and governs it for abstract accusative Case; no visible accusative suffix is required. Abafana is then introduced in Spec-VP, where it receives the external agent role. This VP-internal subject analysis separates the position of thematic interpretation from the finite subject position that will be established later.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the thematic VP with its subject and object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite I takes the completed VP as its complement, forming I′ and an IP whose specifier has not yet been filled. The agent remains in its previously established Spec-VP position. I supplies present-tense interpretation to the predicate and provides the finite head needed for the later nominative and subject-agreement relations. Neither the subject nor the verb has moved at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Place the thematic VP under finite inflection.

values.chain: Raised V and silent V trace
values.movementType: Head adjunction to the immediately higher I

values.linearization: Subject concord precedes ya-, which precedes the verbal stem and final vowel.

relations.relation: Head-trace government and inherited object government

values.headTraceLicensing: The raised verbal head antecedent-governs its trace.
values.objectCase: The verbal chain preserves the object's accusative licensing at the complement position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The previously independent V head moves from the head position of V′ to I, leaving an unpronounced head trace. Movement targets the immediately higher inflectional head, so it does not skip an intervening head. The resulting complex I head is linearized with prefixal inflection before the verbal stem. Its morphological realization is ba-ya-dlal-a, written bayadlala; dlala already contains the final vowel -a, so no additional syntactic final-vowel terminal is introduced. The realization group records the spelling of this complex head rather than treating baya as an independent word. The verbal trace preserves the object's local government relation within V′, and the raised verb governs its head trace.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the verb to inflection and establish the finite verbal word.

values.thetaRole: Agent, retained through the lower chain position

values.agreement: Class-2 Abafana licenses class-2 subject concord ba-.

values.traceStatus: The silent NP trace is locally A-bound, satisfying the GB requirement on an anaphoric NP trace.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Abafana moves from the Spec-VP position shown in the preceding workspace to Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace. This is A-movement into a non-theta position: the NP retains the agent role assigned at its lower position and receives no second theta role. Finite I assigns nominative Case to the raised subject, and the Spec-IP–I relation licenses class-2 agreement ba-. The raised NP A-binds its VP-internal trace, producing a single argument chain with one theta role and one Case. The object remains the selected complement of the verbal trace and is not moved or doubled. The completed structure therefore has the pronounced order Abafana, bayadlala, ibhola. No question, embedding, or independent complementizer is expressed, so the analysis terminates at declarative IP.

cases.sentence: There are three books on the table.

relations.relation: Prepositional selection, theta assignment, and Case licensing

values.interpretation: Three books have their location on the table.

derivationStages.stageRecord: On this reading, the locative phrase predicates a location of three books rather than restricting the noun books. The preposition on selects the table, assigns it the Ground role, and licenses its oblique Case. A silent predication head then combines that PP with three books as its small-clause subject; the books receive the Figure role in the locative relation. PredP is an X-bar implementation of the small clause, not a finite clause. Existential be selects this predication and assigns no accusative Case to its subject. Consequently, three books must obtain Case from the finite clause constructed next. The numeral occupies the nominal specifier, while the determiner the occupies the specifier of the table NP. No movement has occurred.
derivationStages.statement: Build the locative-predication reading: three books are located on the table.

values.mechanism: finite Case is shared through the expletive–associate chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: Present-tense I takes the VP as its complement, and expletive there is base-generated in Spec-IP. There satisfies the finite clause's subject requirement but receives no theta role; it is not a locative expression and has not moved from the PP. Under the GB expletive–associate chain analysis adopted here, finite I licenses nominative through the chain connecting there with three books. The nonfinite predication supplies no intervening finite Case domain. The associate retains the Figure role established in the preceding stage, so the chain has only one thematic member. The associate's plural features determine agreement on I. Neither the associate nor there undergoes A-movement in this derivation.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the finite clause and license the postverbal small-clause subject.

values.traceLicensing: antecedent government by the raised verb

derivationStages.stageRecord: Be raises from its previously established V position and adjoins to I, leaving a silent head trace. This is local V-to-I movement: the selected PredP is inside the verb's complement and is not an intervening head on the upward path. The moved verb governs its trace, forming a single verbal chain. The resulting complex I contains be and the present, third-person-plural inflection already licensed by the associate; their collective exponent is are. The realization association records this inflectional spell-out without replacing the lexical be in the syntax. There remains pronounced in Spec-IP, and three books remains in its original small-clause subject position. The completed structure asserts the presence of three books at the table, with the PP functioning as their predicate. The sentence contains no anaphoric or pronominal dependency requiring a further binding operation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise be to finite I and complete the locative-predication analysis.

cases.sentence: She sent her brother a letter.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Adopt a DP version of X-bar Theory within Government and Binding Theory. Build She as a pronominal DP, her brother as a possessive DP, and a letter as an indefinite DP. Inside the recipient DP, her occupies the possessor position, while a silent possessive D heads the projection containing brother. This D licenses genitive Case on her. The possessive structure is important: her is not an independent object of sent, and brother is not a vocative. The three complete DPs remain separate until their verbal positions are introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the subject, recipient, and theme nominals.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Introduce lexical sent and combine it with a letter as its complement, then place her brother in the specifier of the resulting lower VP. This binary-branching VP-shell analysis distinguishes the higher recipient from the lower theme without inserting an unpronounced to. Once the lower VP is assembled, its lexical predicate assigns Theme to a letter and Recipient to her brother. Adopt the GB double-object commitment that the second object receives inherent objective Case together with its thematic licensing. Sent is introduced as an already inflected past-tense lexical form; this analysis will license that inflection through finite I rather than derive the spelling by affix lowering.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lower double-object VP and its internal arguments.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project a silent upper verbal head with the lower VP as its complement, and place She in the upper VP's specifier. This is the subject's base position, not yet its finite-clause position. The upper head introduces the external Agent argument, interpreted as the sender through its combination with the lower send predicate. The recipient remains in the lower specifier and therefore occupies a structurally higher position than the theme. The silent upper head supplies the landing site required for the next head-movement operation.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the upper VP shell and the subject's thematic position.

values.locality: movement to the immediately higher verbal head
values.representation: pronounced moved head and silent source trace

values.government: the selected lower VP is transparent to government of its specifier

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move sent from the lower V position shown in the preceding workspace and adjoin it to the immediately higher verbal head. The pronounced lexical occurrence retains its identity at the landing site; a silent V trace occupies its former position. This local head movement produces the order sent–her brother–a letter while preserving the lower predicate's thematic and inherent-Case dependencies through the head chain. The resulting upper verbal head governs the recipient across its selected lower VP and assigns structural objective Case to her brother. This Case assignment is to the whole recipient DP, not to the embedded possessive pronoun, whose genitive Case is already licensed.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the lexical verb within the VP shell and license the first object.

values.representation: pronounced moved DP and silent source trace

values.implementation: finite I licenses the lexically inflected verb without V-to-I movement

values.requirement: the subject pronoun is locally free

values.reference: coreference with She is permitted but not required
values.requirement: the possessive pronoun is free within its local possessive DP

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project finite past I over the completed VP shell and add a silent declarative C. Raise She from the previously established upper Spec-VP to Spec-IP, leaving a silent DP trace. The A-chain retains the Agent role at its lower position; its upper position satisfies the finite subject requirement. Finite I then licenses nominative Case on She and licenses the already past-inflected sent in the upper verbal projection. No V-to-I movement or affix-lowering derivation is posited. Finally, apply Principle B: She must be locally free in the finite clause, and possessive her must be free within its local possessive DP, where silent possessive D licenses and governs it. The clause subject is outside that possessive binding domain, so her may refer either to the subject or to another contextually supplied female individual. These referential possibilities do not require distinct constituent structures. The completed double-object structure has her brother as Recipient and a letter as Theme; its pronounced terminals yield the exact input.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the finite declarative clause and establish subject and binding dependencies.
